references.text: The Lord makes a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, a similar theme about God separating His people from the Egyptians.
The Lord distinguishes between the Egyptians and Israel, the same motif concerning God's protection of His people.
Moses asks when the plagues will cease, and Pharaoh says 'tomorrow' - the same time indication 'לְמָחָר' (tomorrow) is used.
God's signs and wonders in Egypt that are to serve as a testimony, related to 'הָאֹת הַזֶּה' (this sign).
The psalm describes the plague of flies that God sent upon the Egyptians, a poetic retelling of this event.
A reference to the flies that came over all Egypt, a historical reminder of the plagues.
Both verses illustrate God's ability to distinguish between peoples in order to preserve a 'new' or 'true' people while others are destroyed.
Clear parallel: God's threat to destroy the people and replace them with a new 'greater' people underscores the distinction between God's plan and human failure.
